title: Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Week 2027
content:
Geneva, Switzerland

The 13th edition of the Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Week (HNPW), co-hosted by OCHA and the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, will take place in Geneva from 2 to 4 March 2027.

Building on the rich discussions of HNPW 2026 around locally led action, resilience building, effective coordination, and innovative financing, HNPW 2027 will continue to provide a unique platform for dialogue, learning, and partnership-building to drive the humanitarian reset and shape the future of humanitarian action.
creator: Elayne Wangalwa
sourceDescription: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Weeks 2025
content:
Geneva, Switzerland

At a time of mounting needs, acute funding constraints and shifting geopolitical dynamics, Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Weeks (HNPW) 2025 brought the global aid community together to explore how the humanitarian system can adapt and better serve people affected by crises.
creator: Elayne Wangalwa
sourceDescription: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Weeks 2026
content:
Geneva, Switzerland

The 12th edition of the Humanitarian Networks and Partnerships Weeks (HNPW) co-hosted by Switzerland and OCHA and brought together 7,800 participants from across the humanitarian community under the theme: Shaping the Humanitarian Reset – From Global Commitments to Local Action. HNPW 2026 encouraged collective reflection on how the humanitarian system must adapt to growing needs, shifting geopolitics and declining resources.
creator: Elayne Wangalwa
sourceDescription: United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs

title: Dr. Mehmet Güllüoğlu
content:
Dr. Güllüoğlu is a senior diplomat and public health professional with two decades of leadership experience in humanitarian assistance, disaster management and international cooperation. He previously worked as Senior Adviser to the President of Türkiye. Before that, he served as Türkiye's Humanitarian Aid Coordinator for the Occupied Palestinian Territory (OPT) to oversee the coordination and monitoring of Türkiye's humanitarian activities in Gaza.

From 2021 to 2024, he served as Ambassador of Türkiye to the United Republic of Tanzania. Between 2017 and 2021, he headed Türkiye's Disaster and Emergency Management Authority, leading a nationwide structure of 81 provincial directorates, 11 response brigades, roughly 6,000 personnel, and 100,000 volunteers. In this role, he helped develop the national volunteer model that proved vital for disaster response and public awareness.
